note: Fictional companies. None of this is run automatically; see README.md.

company.product: Phone app. You photograph the inside of your fridge or cupboard and it suggests dinners you can make from what is there.
company.persona: Someone who gets home at seven, opens the fridge, sees food and still orders delivery.

pains.pain: I have food and nothing to eat.
pains.quote: I stare at the fridge for five minutes and then open the delivery app anyway.

pains.pain: Vegetables go off before I use them.
pains.quote: I threw out a whole bag of spinach again.

approved_claims.wording: Suggests dinners from a photo of what is in your fridge.
Gives three dinner options per photo.
Free for five photos a week.

demo_moments.title: Fridge photo to three dinners
demo_moments.start_state: the camera view pointed at an open fridge
demo_moments.end_state: three dinner cards, each listing the ingredients it spotted

company.constraints: Never claim it saves a stated amount of money. Never call it a nutritionist or a diet tool. Do not say AI in the hook.
company.offer_and_cta: Organic creator posts. Ask: link in bio. No creator codes.

request.title: What to cook when you have food and nothing to eat

must: Open on the fridge moment in the customer's words, not on the app.
Show demo moment d-fridge and hold on the three dinner cards.
Cite c-photo or c-three on the clip that describes what it did.
Name Pantry Lens once, in the last clip, with a link in bio ask.
must_not: Say AI in the hook.
State money saved or a diet benefit.
List more than one feature.
Invent a dish the product suggested with a claim about quality.

company.product: Web and phone app that turns a handful of selfies into professional headshots for a CV or work profile.
company.persona: Someone applying for jobs who has no decent photo and does not want to pay a photographer.

pains.pain: My profile photo is a cropped wedding picture.
pains.quote: My LinkedIn photo is me at a wedding with someone's arm cut off.

approved_claims.wording: Makes headshots from 8 selfies.
Results arrive in about 20 minutes.

company.constraints: Never say results look exactly like you. Never say hiring managers prefer it. AI-generated images must be described as generated.
company.offer_and_cta: Organic creator posts. Ask: link in bio.

request.title: I needed a headshot by Monday
request.linkNotes: Same energy, but for job hunting

reference.subject: an AI app that makes a fake celebrity selfie

hook.spoken: I told my mum I met him at the airport.
hook.on_screen: telling my mum I met him
hook.visual: phone screen of a text thread

why_it_works: comments are about the mum, not the app

keep: a real person's reaction as the payoff

must: Keep what transfers (result on screen within about three seconds, a real reaction as payoff) and say what did not transfer.
Tie the result to the job application problem so the video is not shareable without wanting the product.
Describe the images as generated.
must_not: Script deceiving anyone with a fake image.
Copy any sentence or the mum set-up from the reference.
Claim the headshots look exactly like the creator or that hiring managers prefer them.

company.product: Error tracing for backend services. Groups a production error with the request that caused it and the commit that introduced it.
company.persona: A backend engineer on call for a small team who gets paged and has to work out which deploy broke it.

pains.pain: The stack trace tells me where, not why or since when.
pains.quote: I spend the first twenty minutes of every incident just finding which deploy did it.

pains.pain: Logs are in three places.
pains.quote: I have four tabs open before I have read a single line.

approved_claims.wording: Links each error group to the commit where it first appeared.
Shows the request that triggered the error next to the stack trace.
Supports Node, Python and Go services.

demo_moments.title: Error to commit
demo_moments.end_state: the commit diff that introduced the error, with author and deploy time

company.constraints: Never claim it prevents outages or reduces downtime by any figure. No customer names. No AI claims; the product does not use AI.
company.offer_and_cta: Goal is trial sign-ups from engineers. Ask: search the name or link in bio. Free for one service.

request.title: The first twenty minutes of every incident

must: Use a real artifact as the first background (a stack trace or a wall of logs described generically), then d-commit as the answer.
Sound like an engineer talking to another engineer, with one honest limit (for example the supported languages).
Cite c-commit on the clip that shows the commit.
must_not: Claim reduced downtime, prevented outages or any figure.
Use hype words or stock 'hacker' imagery.
Mention AI.
Name a customer or a competitor's product screen.

company.product: Phone app that reads your card statements and lists every recurring charge so you can see what you are still paying for.
company.persona: Someone in their twenties or thirties who suspects they are paying for things they forgot about and avoids opening their banking app.

pains.pain: I do not know what I am subscribed to.
pains.quote: I found out I had been paying for a meditation app for two years.

pains.pain: Reading statements feels like homework.
pains.quote: I never read these.

approved_claims.wording: Lists every recurring charge found on your connected cards.
Looks back over the last 12 months of statements.
Creator codes give one month of the paid plan free, entered on the last sign-up screen.

demo_moments.title: Recurring charges list
demo_moments.start_state: the home screen after connecting a card
demo_moments.end_state: a list of recurring charges with monthly amounts and a count at the top

company.offer_and_cta: Organic creator posts, some later boosted. Each creator has a code. Ask: say the code once, what it gives and where it is entered.

request.title: The app I forgot I was paying for

must: First person throughout: the creator's own statement, their own small specific sum framed as theirs to adjust.
Say results differ.
Say the code once, what it gives and where it is entered, matching c-code.
Include the on-screen disclosure the constraints require in the first clip.
Show d-list and hold on the count.
must_not: Promise or imply an amount the viewer will save.
Say the app cancels anything.
Address the viewer's financial state in the second person.
Invent a number of subscriptions the product found as a product claim.

company.product: Phone app for short home workouts with a streak counter. Ten-minute sessions, no equipment.
company.persona: Someone who has started and dropped a gym routine several times and feels behind before they begin.

pains.pain: I cannot keep a routine going past two weeks.
pains.quote: I am great for nine days and then I miss one and it is over.

approved_claims.wording: Sessions are ten minutes and need no equipment.
A streak counter shows consecutive days.
One missed day a week does not break the streak.

demo_moments.title: Streak after a session
demo_moments.end_state: the streak counter ticking up by one

company.constraints: No weight loss amounts or timelines. No before and after bodies. Nothing that shames a body. Not a medical product. Write about behaviour and how it felt.
company.offer_and_cta: Organic creator posts. Ask: save or send, or link in bio.

request.title: How I finally kept a routine past two weeks

must: Five to seven slides, text only, hook slide first.
Every non-product slide is a real, useful habit tip on its own.
Product appears once in the middle or later, by what it did (c-freeze or c-streak).
Last slide is the only CTA and gives a reason to save or send.
must_not: Put the product on slide one.
Mention weight, bodies, or results by a date.
Have any spoken line.
Pad the list with filler items.

company.product: Phone app that logs when you fall asleep and wake, and puts daily habits you tag (caffeine, screens, late meals) on the same timeline.
company.persona: Someone who thinks of themselves as a bad sleeper and has not connected it to anything they do.

pains.pain: I am tired and I do not know why.
pains.quote: I assumed I was just a bad sleeper.

approved_claims.wording: Shows your tagged habits and your sleep on one timeline.
Tracks sleep and wake times from phone use; it is an estimate.

demo_moments.title: Habit and sleep timeline
demo_moments.end_state: a tagged habit sitting above that night's sleep bar

company.constraints: Never say it improves, fixes or treats sleep or insomnia. Never give sleep amounts gained. It is an estimate; do not call it accurate. Not medical advice.
company.offer_and_cta: Organic creator posts. Ask: link in bio.

request.title: I thought I was just a bad sleeper

must: One clip, no speech, 45 to 90 words in two or three paragraphs.
At least six {a|b} groups, none containing the product name or a claim.
Product appears once, in the last paragraph, by what it showed (c-timeline).
Reads like one person's thought, with a specific habit and time.
must_not: Say sleep improved because of the app or give hours gained.
Call the tracking accurate.
Use a headline tone or list formatting.

company.product: Joins video calls and produces a summary with who said what and a list of action items when the call ends.
company.persona: Someone a few weeks into a job with back-to-back calls who keeps losing what they agreed to do.

pains.pain: I cannot listen and take notes at once.
pains.quote: I literally cannot listen and write at the same time.

pains.pain: Someone always asks for the notes.
pains.quote: Can you send the notes? I did not take any.

approved_claims.wording: Produces a summary when the call ends.
Pulls out action items with the name of who took each one.
Free for the first ten calls.

demo_moments.title: End of call summary
demo_moments.end_state: a summary with an Action items section showing three items with names

company.constraints: Never claim transcription accuracy figures. Never say it replaces a note taker or assistant. The bot is visible to other participants; do not imply it is hidden.
company.offer_and_cta: Trial sign-ups. Ask: search the name. Free for the first ten calls.

request.title: My manager asked for the notes
request.linkNotes: Same structure, meeting notes instead of skincare

hook.spoken: My dermatologist looked at my bathroom shelf and laughed.
hook.visual: creator holding an armful of bottles

beats.function: the old way, in embarrassing detail
what the expert said to do instead
the product in use, one action

keep: story cold-open with an authority figure reacting
five beats in this order and proportion
product first seen at 54 percent of runtime

must: Five clips in the reference's order with each close to its word count, product first seen a little past halfway.
A cold-open with someone reacting, rebuilt for work (for example a manager or teammate asking for notes).

Claim accuracy or that it replaces a person.
Run more than about 20 percent over the reference's length.

company.product: Language app built on short spoken conversations with a tutor voice, corrected as you go. Spanish, Italian and Portuguese.
company.persona: Someone with a trip or a partner's family coming up who has done lessons before and still cannot hold a conversation.

pains.pain: I know words and cannot speak.
pains.quote: I have a 400 day streak on another app and I froze ordering a coffee.

approved_claims.wording: Lessons are spoken conversations, not tapping answers.
Corrects your sentence out loud after you say it.
Available for Spanish, Italian and Portuguese.

demo_moments.title: Spoken correction
demo_moments.start_state: a conversation screen with the mic on
demo_moments.user_action: says a sentence with a mistake
demo_moments.end_state: the corrected sentence shown and played back

company.constraints: No fluency timelines. Do not name other apps. Do not claim creators are fluent.
company.offer_and_cta: The company runs a comment flow: viewers comment the word PARLA and get a link by message. Use that as the ask.

request.title: 400 day streak and I froze ordering a coffee

must: Use the customer's own phrase or situation in the opening.
Show d-correct.
Close with the comment PARLA flow as the single ask.
Include one honest limit or moment of doubt.
must_not: Name another app.
Promise fluency or a timeline.
Have the creator claim months of use or fluency.
Add link in bio on top of the comment ask.
